RIO A + RIO B

Populated from your two sheets

22 slots100 channels56 devices44 spares

All 56 named devices and all 26 handwritten cable numbers are included. The other 30 cable-number fields are blank because no number was written in the source.

Connections included

82 conductors are routed: 54 on standard AI, 12 on two-channel AI, and 16 DQ signal leads. Black connects to − and white to + on two-wire inputs, following your example.

Pin assignments still needed

The 7 RTD labels have all four colored conductors ready for manual wiring. The sheets do not map those colors to M+, M−, I+, and I−. The 16 DQ black returns are ready for manual connection to the individual 0V terminals.

Source interpretation

Four-channel AI groups use the supplied AI RTD artwork; two-channel AI groups use Ex-AI artwork. The sheet itself labels these groups AI. Spare groups use the same channel-count convention. No AQ channel assignments appear in the sheets.

The duplicate blank RIO A Slot 5 block is merged with its populated rows. Slot 5 tags are corrected to rioa.slot5.ai0…ai7. .wire_ok entries are retained as status metadata, not extra physical channels.
A QUICK TOUR

Your wiring workspace

01

Place your components

Add a module or a 2-wire / 4-wire cable label. Drag it anywhere on the grid. Use Properties to edit names, cable numbers, label side, width, and height.

02

Make your connections

Click a conductor dot on a cable label, then a channel port on a module. You can also drag between ports. A new wire gets an initial path, then stays in place. Moving a component keeps its wires attached.

03

Adjust one wire at a time

Select a wire, then drag any segment or square handle. Other wire paths stay fixed. Auto-route is off by default. Use Auto-route this wire for one connection, or Auto-route all to replace every path. Turn on Auto-route for live routing while arranging components. Undo restores previous paths.

04

Save and share

Save project downloads an editable JSON file, including your wire paths and routing preference. Open restores it. Export PNG keeps the same layout with an optional transparent background.

Copy and paste: Select a device label or connector tag, or Shift-click several to select a group. Use the Copy and Paste toolbar buttons, or Ctrl/Cmd+C and Ctrl/Cmd+V. Copies keep their names, sizes, colors, and side settings and are ready to wire. Device cable numbers are preserved; tags with matching names remain linked.

Connector tags: Tags with the same name represent a virtual connection. Wire each tag where you need it, then select a tag and choose a matching tag in Properties to jump to its location.
